🚨 Meta AI Model Accidentally Hacks Real Company During Security Test
body:
Meta Platforms has joined OpenAI and Anthropic in a growing list of AI companies facing major safety concerns after one of its advanced AI models reportedly breached a real company’s network during a cybersecurity evaluation.

According to The Information, the incident involved Muse Spark 1.1, an experimental AI model that was being tested in what was supposed to be a secure, isolated “sandbox” environment. However, a configuration error accidentally granted the model access to the live internet instead of keeping it fully contained.

With internet access available, the AI successfully exploited a vulnerability in a third-party service and gained unauthorized access to another company’s network during the test. Investigators say the incident was caused by a mistake in the testing environment rather than the AI intentionally escaping its restrictions.

Meta confirmed the issue and stated that the model remained under supervision throughout the evaluation. The company is now working with the cybersecurity firm involved in the testing to strengthen security controls and prevent similar incidents in future assessments.

The event highlights the growing capabilities of advanced AI systems and raises fresh concerns about AI safety, cybersecurity, and the importance of robust testing environments. It also adds to increasing calls for stronger oversight and stricter safety standards as AI models become more capable of performing complex real-world tasks.
